text.p: Premium coffee retailer Starbucks Corp. said Friday it raised prices on its coffee products to reflect higher coffee bean costs around the world.
The Seattle-based retailer said it raised the price of a cup by 5 cents and the price of a pound of ground beans by 30 cents. Prices currently vary by location and coffee type.
In some stores, a medium-sized cup of coffee went from $1.15 to $1.20 and a pound of Sumatra blend from $4.80 to $5.10.

"Over the past few months, worldwide coffee prices have significantly increased," the company said. "After carefully monitoring and evaluating coffee costs, we have made a decision to increase prices in order to reflect the higher cost of the green coffee we buy, roast and sell.

"We waited as long as we could to make this pricing decision, but coffee costs remained at a high level longer than expected," Starbucks added. "Even though we are raising prices we are only taking the minimal increase to offset higher costs."

The move follows a sharp rise in coffee prices recently, fuelled in part by heavy rains in South America and labour unrest in Colombia. In the last three months coffee futures prices have doubled, putting pressure on retailers to raise prices or risk hurting profits.
